# A mean with its calculation

The observations are $x=(2,4,6,8)$, so the sample mean is

$$
\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
=\frac{2+4+6+8}{4}=5.
$$

```{r analysis, echo=TRUE}
x <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
n <- length(x)
sample_mean <- mean(x)
sample_sd <- sd(x)
standard_error <- sample_sd / sqrt(n)
c(mean = sample_mean, standard_error = standard_error)
```

The computed mean is `r sample_mean`, and its standard error is
`r round(standard_error, 4)`. The calculation and this sentence use the same
R variables.

The Python and Node chunks below also run in this document build. The Node
chunk uses a simple TypeScript type annotation supported by the Node 22
runtime; it is not a general TypeScript project build.

```{python, echo=TRUE}
python_values = [2, 4, 6, 8]
print("Python mean:", sum(python_values) / len(python_values))
```

```{node, echo=TRUE}
const typedMean: number = [2, 4, 6, 8].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / 4;
console.log("Typed Node mean:", typedMean);
```

# Matrix notation

For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$ and
$v=\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}$, ordinary matrix multiplication gives

$$
Av=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}4\\10\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The next plot is generated during the same PDF build.

```{r figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=5, fig.height=3, fig.cap="The four observations and their mean."}
plot(seq_along(x), x, pch = 19, xlab = "Observation", ylab = "Value")
abline(h = sample_mean, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
```
